what: Close gh #54: `prismis-cli context bootstrap` prints a portable interview prompt a new user pastes into any chatbot; the chatbot asks about their interests, what they skip and the sources they already read, and returns a context.md in the sections prismis reads plus the `prismis-cli source add` commands for the feeds they named.
why: context.md drives every priority decision, but a first run writes a sample context with someone else's interests (defaults.py DEFAULT_CONTEXT_MD: AI/LLM, Rust, SQLite, React), so a new user's first fetch is scored against the wrong person. The existing `:context suggest` only refines a context from flagged items; nothing helps from zero. The new-user probe on 2026-10-07 also showed verify failing on 'no active sources' after setup, so the same interview that collects interests can hand back the user's feeds as ready-to-run commands.
decided: `prismis-cli context bootstrap` prints the prompt to stdout and nothing else, so it can be piped or copied; it needs no daemon, no network and no LLM call.

The prompt interviews in 6 to 10 questions: what the user wants to know about first, what they follow casually, what they never want to see, and the blogs, subreddits and YouTube channels they already read.

The prompt's output spec is a context.md with exactly the sections prismis reads: '## High Priority Topics', '## Medium Priority Topics', '## Low Priority Topics' (required by the context validator) and '## Not Interested' (which the evaluator's prompt maps to no priority), each a list of specific topics, followed by one `prismis-cli source add <url>` line per feed the user named, using the rss, reddit:// and youtube:// forms prismis accepts.
The prompt text lives in one place in the CLI package as a Python string, so it ships with every install without package-data configuration and there is no second copy to drift.
The first-run next-steps text and the README Quick Start point at the command in place of the hand-written sample.
A test fails if the prompt's output spec names a section the daemon does not read or omits one it requires.
